questions.evidence: Jeremiah Barker was my new master's name

questions.q: How does Beauty describe the Barker family?
choices: The happiest, merriest family he ever knew
questions.evidence: I never knew such a happy, merry family before or since

questions.q: Where had Captain gone when he was young?
choices: To the Crimean War with a cavalry officer
To a farm in the country
questions.evidence: he went to the Crimean War

questions.q: What new name did Jerry give Beauty?
questions.evidence: We'll call him 'Jack', after the old one

questions.q: What did Jerry mean by giving Beauty "the benefit of the doubt" about his broken knees?
choices: He would not blame Beauty since nobody knew whose fault it was
He would sell Beauty if he fell again
He thought Beauty had fallen on purpose
He would make Beauty work twice as hard
questions.evidence: as long as I don't know I shall give him the benefit of the doubt

choices: With no check-rein and no curb, just a plain snaffle
questions.evidence: There was no check-rein, no curb, nothing but a plain ring snaffle

questions.q: What did Governor Grant say after looking Beauty over?
choices: He was the right sort for Jerry and worth what he cost
He would be good for a funeral
questions.evidence: He's the right sort for you, Jerry

questions.q: What made Beauty's first week as a London cab horse so trying?
choices: The noise, hurry, and crowds of London
questions.evidence: the noise, the hurry, the crowds of horses, carts, and carriages

questions.q: The stalls had two "movable" bars fixed across the back. What does "movable" mean here?
choices: Able to be put up or taken down
questions.evidence: he just took off our halters and put up the bars, and thus we could turn about

questions.q: What does this chapter mostly show about Jerry?
choices: He is a good driver who cares for his horses as much as himself
He is a strict master who works his horses too hard
He is new to horses and makes many mistakes
He only cares about earning money
questions.evidence: he took as much thought for his horses as he did for himself
